autonomy_models.capability_ladder: autonomy:R0 .. autonomy:R9 -- a property of each capability
autonomy_models.warning: These are different scales on different objects. Never render one as a position on the other, and never compare them.

staleness_note: This file deliberately carries no timestamp: a clock here would make every sync commit a file whose only change is the time. Read `generated_at` from `.colaberry/manifest.json` and label it "last changed", not "last checked".

authority.ceiling_reason: Identifying the list is read-only. Contacting anyone on it is prospect contact needing live_email, which is default-denied, so the pilot ceiling applies to producing the list and never to working it.

reasons: human_decision_required_at_every_level
authority.ceiling_reason: Reconciliation marks people paid and activates subscriptions, so the write is a human decision. Shadow mode is the ceiling and is genuinely available here because dryRun gives an approved reference stream: the agent can state what it would link and be compared against the deterministic reconciler's own dry run.

The existing implementation is read-only by explicit design, so a supervised production pilot of the watch is the natural ceiling. R7 is prohibited because the only actions a finding implies are charging, cancelling or changing a schedule, all of which are human decisions.

reasons: human_decision_required_at_every_level
authority.ceiling_reason: A comp sets the price to zero for a named person, which is a discount, and discounting is explicitly forbidden to an agent. The agent may report who holds a comp and why; granting or revoking stays a human decision.

The scope of this capability is unknown, and an autonomy ceiling over an undefined scope would be a fabrication. R0, defining the workflow and the human decisions, is the only honest level until the duty list exists. This is deliberately the lowest ceiling in the matrix.

reasons: human_decision_required_at_every_level
authority.ceiling_reason: Issuing a payment link creates a payable charge against a named person, which is a financial commitment. R5 shadow mode would require a reference stream of real link issuances to compare against and none exists as an approved reference outcome; R6 and above is a production money action and is prohibited. The agent may describe and verify the flow in a sandbox and never issue a production link.

Assembling and maintaining the follow-through list is read-only, and shadow mode against Roselyn's own judgement of who is genuinely stuck is reachable once she can see the list. The contact itself needs live_email and stays human, so nothing above R5 applies.

Sourcing and scoring write no money and contact nobody, so shadow mode against the human's own accept/reject decisions is the honest ceiling. R6 and above would turn the recommendation into an action, and the approval step is the control that kept the legacy agent safe.

reasons: human_decision_required_at_every_level
authority.ceiling_reason: This is the control on which every other capability's promotion depends, so the agent's role in it is to present and record, never to decide. It cannot exceed answering questions about the queue's contents, and it is blocked outright until the manager has a surface.

A routing label is reversible, moves no money and reaches no prospect, so a separately approved supervised production pilot is defensible. It stops at R6 because overwriting a human's manual routing is an authorized-action-class question Roselyn has not been asked.

The packet is a document, but what it authorizes is prospect contact, which needs live_email. The legacy agent auto-approved high-scoring recommendations with no named approver, so capping at stateful sandbox work is what keeps the approval gate real rather than nominal.

Detection and reporting are read-only, so a supervised production pilot of the watch is defensible. It stops short of R7 because the legacy agents' auto-retry, auto-heal and auto-resolve are exactly the action classes nobody has authorized, and because billingHealthCheck.ts:8-11 states the standing rule that a watchdog which can act can cause the incident it was built to catch.

reasons: human_decision_required_at_every_level
authority.ceiling_reason: This capability records money and grants paid entitlement; it is the authoritative write for revenue. The agent may observe and, in shadow mode, state what the confirmation outcome should have been and compare it to what the deterministic handler did, because that reference stream exists. It may never perform the write: production_database is default-denied and a wrong confirmation grants or denies a paid seat.

Detecting an identity mismatch is read-only and is exactly the check that would have caught three students sitting unlinked. A supervised production pilot of the detection is defensible; correcting a mismatch touches who gets billed, so it stays a human decision and R7 is prohibited.

The watch reads and reports only. A supervised production pilot is defensible because the thing it watches is already happening whether or not anyone is looking. Adding a dedup store is a schema change that goes through review, so R7 is prohibited.

The digest reports money but moves none, so a supervised production pilot is reasonable once the unavailable-not-zero rule is proven. It stops below R7 because changing recipients or cadence is a manager decision and the send goes through the existing deterministic sender, not the agent.

Stage and temperature are reversible CRM state that moves no money and reaches no prospect, so a supervised production pilot of proposing moves is defensible. It stops at R6 because writing a stage change without review can silently overwrite a human's judgement about a live deal.

The audit only reads and reports, so a supervised production pilot is defensible and immediately useful. Changing a price is explicitly forbidden to the agent, so R7 is prohibited: the audit reports drift and a human decides which number is right.

reasons: human_decision_required_at_every_level
authority.ceiling_reason: A draft is a document, but this domain is recorded as the highest external-side-effect risk in the fleet, and the cadence that protects it is that a human sends. live_email is default-denied, so the agent is capped at stateful sandbox drafting; human_decision stays true because a draft states prices and therefore makes a financial representation.

reasons: human_decision_required_at_every_level
authority.ceiling_reason: Answering from approved knowledge is the textbook R2 capability, and because this surface is rep-facing rather than prospect-facing a shadow-mode comparison against Roselyn's own answers is reachable. It stops at R5 because every answer states a price, and a price stated to a rep is repeated to a prospect: the human decision flag is set for that reason even though no money moves in this capability.

reasons: human_decision_required_at_every_level
authority.ceiling_reason: Assembling a packet writes no money, but an offer is a price representation, so human_decision is true and the ceiling stops at sandbox work. A production pilot would mean the agent's packet reaching a buyer, which is both a price commitment and prospect contact.

reasons: human_decision_required_at_every_level
authority.ceiling_reason: A refund moves money out and is irreversible. This is the hardest stop in the domain: the agent may answer questions about the refund ledger and the stated policy and, at most, hand a human a recommendation to consider. It never touches the refund path, not even in a sandbox, because the refund policy itself is recorded as drafted and pending approval (salesHubCoryController.ts:33) and exercising an unapproved policy is not a sandbox detail.

Building the worklist reads money data and writes none. Shadow mode against Roselyn's own daily list is reachable. Every row's action is a contact or a charge, both of which stay human, so nothing above R5 applies.

The reminder tells a customer money is about to be taken, which makes the copy and the timing a financial communication. It reaches a real customer, so it needs live_email and is default-denied to the agent. The agent may compute who is due and verify idempotency in a sandbox; the send stays with the existing deterministic job.

Reporting is read-only and moves no money, so a separately approved supervised production pilot of report drafting is defensible. It stops below R7 because no reporting figure may be published without a human reading it, and because a fabricated revenue figure is the single most damaging output this domain can produce.

The guard only reads and reports, so a supervised production pilot is defensible and valuable. It stops below R7 because fixing a violation is a code change that goes through review, and because the agent must never be the thing that decides a revenue definition.

Counting seats is read-only, and a supervised production pilot of the count and the disagreement flag is defensible. It stops below R7 because changing max_seats or a published scarcity claim is a commercial decision, and because an overstated seat claim made to a prospect is a representation risk.

Detection is harmless, but the legacy behaviour ends in enrolling a real person into an outbound recovery sequence, which is prospect contact requiring live_email. The agent is therefore capped at stateful sandbox work and the contact stays human.

reasons: human_decision_required_at_every_level
authority.ceiling_reason: Cancelling alters subscription state and stops a charge; getting it half-done either keeps charging a cancelled member or stops charging an active one. It is a human decision, and because the cancellation terms are not yet approved the agent is held to answering questions only.

reasons: human_decision_required_at_every_level
authority.ceiling_reason: Starting a checkout creates a charge and activation mutates subscription state and billing dates. Both are financial actions reserved to a human. Sandbox verification is the ceiling; a production pilot of either would be the agent charging a customer.

Analysis is read-only and shadow mode against actual lapses is a genuine reference stream: the agent's risk list can be scored against who actually lapsed. It stops at R5 because the action implied by every row is a contact or a retention offer, both human decisions.

reasons: human_decision_required_at_every_level
authority.ceiling_reason: A redemption allocates prepaid paid entitlement to a named person, and pricing a team license sets a price. Both are financial decisions. Sandbox verification of the idempotency and over-allocation guards is the ceiling; allocation and pricing in production stay human.

authority_rule.rule: A capability approved above autonomy:R2 with no granted tools is forced back down to autonomy:R2, with the reason no_tool_grants. Tool grants are the throttle.
authority_rule.note: When this binds nothing, say so in words. It means no capability in this domain has been approved above autonomy:R2 yet, not that the rule is absent or that the panel failed.

governance.disclosure: A filed request grants nothing. Status is what a named human decided, and a pending row means nobody has decided yet.

verification.disclosure: A criterion counts as passing when it is marked in `.colaberry/progress.json` in this repository. The verifier reads that file on every sync and records what it found. A story showing 0 of N is not a rejection: nothing has been claimed yet.

stories.title: STORY-000 · Build your Command Center
reasons: None of the 6 acceptance criteria are marked as passing yet.
outstanding: Given the Command Center, when it is opened, then all six panels render and each one names the endpoint it read.
Given a panel whose endpoint returned nothing, when it renders, then it says so in words and is visibly distinct from a panel that is still loading.
Given the autonomy ladder panel, when it renders, then all ten rungs are present with the owner's wording, and each capability's ceiling is marked against the rung it stops at.

Given the autonomy ladder panel, when a capability's authority is shown, then the page shows the effective authority `effectiveAuthority()` returns rather than the level the capability record asks for, and names the `no_tool_grants` rule with the number of capabilities it currently constrains, saying so in words when that number is zero.
Given the governance panel, when a tool request is shown, then nothing on the page states or implies that filing it granted anything.
Trust -- no panel shows a number, a grant, a rung or a result this domain has not actually produced.

not_recorded.reason: The platform does not store who set an agent's autonomy level. `ai_agents` carries `autonomy_level_set_at` and `autonomy_level_source` but no `set_by` column, so the time and whether a person chose it are known and the identity is not. Do not render a name here.
